sections.html:
Deeds are recorded in Windsor, in the courthouse at King and Dundee streets. The register's office is on the first floor. Visitors use 108 Dundee Street, and mail goes to PO Box 340, Windsor, NC 27983.

The office is open from 8:30 to 5:00, but recording stops at 4:30. A deed that arrives at a quarter to five waits until the next morning. Electronic recording is accepted, so closing attorneys can file without driving to Windsor. Holidays and bad weather may close the doors, so call ahead if timing is tight.

The Bertie register keeps deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, maps and military records. The office is elected every second year and works under Chapter 161 of the General Statutes.

A buyer's priority depends on filing. G.S. 47-18 says a deed nobody has recorded loses to lien creditors and to purchasers who paid value, and the date of registration sets the order. Until the deed reaches the courthouse, a rival claim can get ahead of the buyer.

  • Records are filed by name, so the office cannot look up an owner from a street address.
  • For an address search, call the tax assessor's mapping line at (252) 794-5311.
  • Once a paper is recorded, anyone can ask for a copy at the counter, by letter or by phone. Military discharge forms are the exception because access to them is limited.

Charges track the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, which the county fee page reproduces. A standard instrument costs $26.00 through page 15, with $4.00 added for each page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage runs $64.00 through page 35 on the same $4.00 add-on.

  • Second instrument in one document: $10.00
  • Format failure: $25.00 on top of the filing fee
  • Satisfaction of a mortgage: no charge

Pay the fee before filing; the statute makes that schedule the only filing charge. If your document has an odd page count, phone (252) 794-5309 before you send it.

sections.h2: Excise tax the seller pays at recording
sections.html:
North Carolina puts an excise tax on the seller: $1.00 for every $500 of price or value, and a leftover fraction of $500 counts as a full unit. The register collects it before the deed is filed.

Half of what the register collects stays in the county general fund and half goes to the Department of Revenue. A parcel that sits in two counties is taxed in the one holding more of its value. The closing attorney figures the amount from the contract price and usually takes it out of your proceeds.

A resolution adopted in April 1991 under G.S. 161-30 took effect June 1, 1991. The register may not take any map or instrument affecting real property unless two items appear on its face: a name and address for returning the document, and the grantee's permanent mailing address.

Format rules apply as well. Use letter or legal paper, black type on white, nothing smaller than 9 point, one side only, and leave a 3 inch blank band at the top of page one. A paper that misses the format is still recorded once the $25.00 non-standard fee is paid, and the register may waive the fee for a slightly small but legible font.

Before you send a deed to Windsor, confirm that it is signed and notarized, that both addresses appear on page one, and that the fee and transfer tax are ready.

sections.h2: Old land records and inherited tracts
sections.html:
Bertie Precinct became a county in 1722, when it separated from Chowan County, and the register's land and grant records start that same year. The original county was large. It took in what are now Tyrrell, Edgecombe, Northampton and Hertford counties, and by 1780 it had been divided into roughly its present shape.

If you are selling an inherited farm tract, this can matter. A chain of title that begins in colonial grants may run through Bertie books even when the land now lies in a neighboring county, so a title search can reach back much farther than the online window. The online index starts in 1977 and also supports a search by book number from Book 600. Call the office about anything older.

sections.h2: Other services at the Windsor counter
sections.html:
The register's staff also issue marriage licenses, swear in notaries, and sell birth and death certificates, so the counter can be busy. A marriage license applicant must arrive before 4:00 p.m., an hour ahead of the recording cutoff. Notary oaths need no appointment, and a new notary may bring the green transmittal letter from the Secretary of State.

Two items at the counter are cash only: the $60.00 marriage license and the $24.00 statewide birth certificate service for people born anywhere in North Carolina from 1971 onward. When you call, ask how the office wants payment for a recording.

Draw up a new deed with an attorney's help, sign it before a notary, and bring it to the office with the fee. That is the register's own answer for a name change.

A land contract works differently. Under Chapter 47H, the seller must record the contract, or a short memorandum of it, within five business days, and the purchaser can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing.

Paid-off loans can leave a loose end. Ask the lender for a satisfaction and have it recorded. That costs nothing and clears the title check before a sale.

sections.h2: How the register fits into a sale
sections.html:
Your closing attorney or title agent searches the records, files the new deed and any lender's deed of trust, and pays the transfer tax out of the settlement. Most sellers never set foot in the office.

Property taxes are the one title item that lives elsewhere. Unpaid bills are a lien and are cleared with the tax collector, as covered in our Bertie County property tax guide. Gaps from older paperwork, such as a mortgage never released or an estate never opened, get fixed by recording the missing document before closing.

One courthouse serves the whole county, so a parcel in any of the eight towns is recorded at the same counter. Whoever buys, the new deed still ends up in the Windsor books.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Bertie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call (252) 794-5309, or send a fax to (252) 794-5374. The office is at 108 Dundee Street in Windsor.

faqs.q: What is the last time to record a deed in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Recording closes at 4:30 p.m., thirty minutes before the office does. Electronic recordings are accepted too.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a standard Bertie County deed?
faqs.a: Through 15 pages the charge is $26.00, then $4.00 for each extra page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 through 35 pages.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Bertie County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $1.00 per $500 of value to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How do I find the owner of a Bertie County street address?
faqs.a: Call the tax assessor's mapping office at (252) 794-5311. The register indexes by name, so an address alone will not work there.
